name: Amzi
overview: Amzi was a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the son of Zechariah according to Nehemiah 11:12. His role or activities beyond this lineage are not detailed in Scripture. As a Levite, he belonged to the priestly tribe set apart for service to God.
namesAndTitles: The name Amzi is a proper name meaning '[possibly] [Y-H-V-H is] my strength,' reflecting a common biblical theme of God as the source of strength. This meaning is derived from the Hebrew root and is noted in Nehemiah 11:12. The name was not explicitly given by God but carries spiritual significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Amzi was the son of Zechariah and infers that Pelaliah was his father, as mentioned in Nehemiah 11:12. Beyond these relationships, no additional family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Amzi's significance lies primarily in his identification within the Levitical lineage, highlighting the continuity of priestly families after the return from exile. His mention in Nehemiah 11:12 situates him in the post-exilic community restoration, emphasizing the importance of the Levites in reestablishing worship and covenant faithfulness. While not a prominent biblical figure with recorded deeds, his inclusion underscores God's faithfulness to His covenant through faithful descendants.
